verdicts.matching_evidence: The $\chi^2_n(\theta)$ template equation includes a factor of 2 in the denominator ($2\hat{\sigma}^2(\theta)$). The canonical definition of the Pearson/reduced $\chi^2$ statistic is $\frac{1}{n} \sum \frac{(x - \mu)^2}{\sigma^2}$. Including the 2 in the denominator makes the expression identical to the negative log-likelihood of a Gaussian error distribution, but it is mathematically non-standard to label it directly as a $\chi^2$ statistic.
